tariff-pass-through.limits: Pass-through and the size of these effects differ by product, market and period; the studies cited concern particular tariff episodes, so their estimates are not figures for another tariff.
tariff-pass-through.mechanism: A tariff is a tax collected on covered imports. Studies of recent US tariffs found that the duty was passed through almost fully into the duty-inclusive prices paid for the imports, so the cost fell on domestic importers and buyers rather than on foreign exporters, and it raised the prices of both intermediate inputs and final goods. Firms that use covered goods as inputs can therefore face higher costs, imports of covered goods tend to fall, and supply chains may be reorganised; partners that retaliate impose similar costs on the other side's exports.
